performance.source_note: Paired benchmark uses final production source. Subsequent changes only adjust the TSYNC test wait, docs and version pin; installed metadata build is separately smoke-tested.

performance_interpretation: Three alternating unprofiled pairs per CPU count and filter mode; 30 complete policy-management rounds per thread. Raw samples are retained.
Thread creation, target directory opens and optional TSYNC precede the timed release. Each round loads, queries identity, attaches, queries IDs, closes/reopens, replaces, detaches and checks old IDs.
Large gains remove BPF cohort returns, not device I/O costs; no Firefox, Docker startup or Geekbench speedup is inferred.
One-CPU medians remain near 1.2 ms. Three short samples do not establish a general improvement or absence of small regressions.
Native Linux reference is an ARM64 CI guest with six provisioned CPUs; twelve threads are oversubscribed. No CPU pinning. macOS has no equivalent Linux BPF syscall.
Trames implements a bounded device-program subset, while native Linux uses its full BPF verifier and object machinery; lower times do not imply full BPF equivalence or general native performance.
The initial timing run overlapped Linux affected-check compilation and is retained separately; the reported medians use the subsequent run after those jobs finished.
Final BPF and target-open cohort-return entries are absent. Aggregate service counts can include other calls; they are not represented as globally zero.
corrected_failures: Moving policy entry exposed target cgroup opens as a remaining joined dependency. Original cgroup directory/control paths now execute through shared filesystem identities, including relative dirfd and deleted/recreated targets.
Concurrent cgroup removal could invalidate the ID between target lookup and hierarchy indexing. Recheck existence inside the attachment transaction; return the original ENODEV result.

The existing TSYNC test assumed four global instruction budgets guaranteed peer scheduling and could also stop after only the first observation. The isolated original test passed; the corrected test waits for all three observations under a five-second bound, retaining source/no-service assertions.
An early restricted host test run denied loopback sockets. The authorized local run and complete runtime workflow passed; no production networking change was made.

New path-test setup initially omitted the proc provider required by the existing source resolver and selected a pids file without enabling that controller. Corrected the test setup; the capability-less boundary remains unchanged.
validation_reuse: Both complete runtime workflows passed before the final cgroup-path dependency fix. Final affected VFS/Linux ABI, process and strict checks plus iPad builds and the real guest matrix cover that fix. Mac process suite passed all 394 cases; Linux affected suite passed 393 and failed only the existing timing-sensitive TSYNC observer, whose corrected targeted retry passes (3 unrelated cases ignored on each host). No full suite rerun is attributed to the test-wait-only change. Unchanged stage-59 product/HVF tests and earlier instruction/graphics/Go/Docker acceptance are reused, not claimed as newly run.
physical_ipad_acceptance: Device/simulator compile checks only; no new physical iPad deployment.
known_unattributed_issue: Stage-56 intermittent Docker cleanup timeout remains unattributed. No Firefox or Docker acceptance rerun is claimed.
